sections.html:
Clark County is in southern Indiana on the north bank of the Ohio River, directly across from Louisville, Kentucky. Jeffersonville is both the county seat and the largest city.

The county covers 376.45 square miles, of which 372.86 is land. The terrain is low rolling hills, and the western part is cut by drainages. The highest point, 1,030 feet, is a ridge west-northwest of Henryville. Other places you will see on Clark County deeds include Clarksville, Charlestown, Sellersburg, Henryville, Marysville and Speed.

Charlestown held the county seat for decades before Jeffersonville took it back in the 1800s. Clark Regional Airport serves the county, and Jeffersonville's position across the river from Louisville gives it quick access to a much larger metro area.

sections.h2: What is the history of Clark County?
sections.html:
Clark County was formed on February 3, 1801, and named for General George Rogers Clark. Settlement began in 1783, and Clarksville, founded in 1784, was the first authorized American settlement in the Northwest Territory.

Jeffersonville grew around Fort Finney, built in 1786 near where the Kennedy Bridge stands today. Shipbuilding began there in 1819, and James Howard's shipyards started in 1832. Those yards later became Jeffboat, once the largest inland shipbuilder in the country. Jeffboat closed in 2018 after employing over 13,000 people at its peak, and the city announced plans in 2022 to redevelop the 80-acre site.

Charlestown also matters to the county story. The Indiana Arsenal, built nearby in 1940, produced smokeless powder in World War II and employed up to 20,000 workers.

sections.h2: What does the Clark County economy depend on?
sections.html:
Clark County has moved from river and heavy industry to a mix of health care, education, finance, logistics and manufacturing. Largest employers in Jeffersonville, as of 2020, included Greater Clark County Schools at about 1,600 employees and Norton Clark Hospital at about 1,500.

  • Heartland Payment Systems, about 850 employees
  • Republic Bank and Trust of Indiana, about 721
  • The U.S. Census Bureau's National Processing Center, which employs 1,200 to more than 6,000 people depending on the season
  • Kitchen Kompact, a cabinet maker with nearly 300 workers

The older industrial base was broad. Ford Plate Glass was established in 1876, the Louisville Cement Company operated in Speed, and Colgate-Palmolive ran on the Clarksville riverfront from the 1920s until early 2008.

River Ridge sits on land from the former Indiana Army Ammunition Plant and now hosts manufacturing, aerospace, automotive, food and beverage, life sciences and logistics companies. Interstate 65 has shaped growth since the 1950s, when it encouraged subdivisions and shopping centers.

The Big Four Bridge, a former rail bridge opened for walkers and cyclists in 2014, draws about 1.5 million crossings a year and has made the Jeffersonville riverfront a destination.

sections.h2: Which Jeffersonville areas come up in Clark County sales?
sections.html:
Jeffersonville includes several areas with their own history, and a seller's parcel may sit in any of them. Port Fulton is a historic area now inside the city, where Jefferson General Hospital and the Howard Shipyards once stood. Oak Park was annexed in 2008, a move that brought the city's population to nearly 50,000.

The downtown and riverfront area holds restaurants, shops and Big Four Station plaza. The NoCo Arts and Cultural District is also in the city. The 2020 census counted 49,447 residents, up from 44,953 in 2010 and 27,362 in 2000.

That growth, much of it from annexation, means tax districts vary across city limits. Check which taxing district your parcel falls in, since the bill combines county, municipal and school levies.

sections.h2: How much does Ohio River flooding and severe weather matter in Clark County?
sections.html:
Flood and storm history is a real factor for Clark County homes. The 1937 flood covered about 90% of Jeffersonville, cut electricity and blocked access roads, and a levee failed during the event.

Wind is the other recorded hazard. The March 2 and 3, 2012 tornado outbreak heavily damaged Marysville and Henryville. A home in either area may have been rebuilt or repaired since then, so a buyer's inspector will ask for permits and repair records.

If your house sits near the river or a creek, ask your insurer about flood coverage and keep any elevation or damage paperwork.

sections.h2: How do Clark County property tax payments work?
sections.html:
Clark County taxes are paid to the county treasurer in two installments, generally due May 10 and November 10, with paper bills mailed in early April. The state due date page showed May 11 and November 10 for 2026.

The treasurer's office is at 300 Corporate Drive, Suite 105, Jeffersonville, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed from noon to 1 p.m. The phone number is 812-285-6205. Mailed payments go to PO Box 1689, Evansville, IN 47706, and the county asks you to include Copy A or Copy B of the bill and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for a receipt.

  • Card payments: 2.25% plus $1.50 per transaction
  • E-check up to $99,999: $1.50 per transaction
  • Duplicate bill: $1.00 per parcel
  • Payment without the barcoded coupon: $1.00 per parcel

Several local banks accept payment during collection season, but only with the bill in hand, only for accounts with no delinquency, and only by the due date.

sections.h2: What are the Clark County property tax appeal steps?
sections.html:
Indiana's state deadline for a Form 130 appeal is June 15 of the year the county sends the assessment notice, or of the year the tax bill is mailed when no Form 11 is sent. You file one petition per parcel with the assessing official.

After filing, the assessor schedules an informal meeting and reports the result to the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals. State guidance says the board must hold its hearing within 180 days of the petition, with at least 30 days of mailed notice. A $50 penalty can apply if you skip the hearing without a valid continuance or withdrawal. If you disagree with the board, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

sections.h2: How does a Clark County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Real property with delinquent taxes is offered at a tax certificate sale run by the Clark County Treasurer. A winning bidder receives a lien through a Tax Sale Certificate issued by the County Auditor.

The owner has one year from the sale date to redeem the property by paying the amounts set by Indiana Code, including interest. If it is not redeemed, the bidder may seek a tax deed. Property listings are published at sriservices.com, and the county recommends legal advice for bidders.

The late penalty before that stage is 5% of the delinquent tax if you pay within 30 days and have no earlier delinquency, and 10% otherwise.

sections.h2: What do Clark County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Clark County sellers often face deferred repairs, inherited houses and landlord exits, and each of these carries tax questions. Here is a short checklist.

  • Request the current balance from the treasurer before choosing a closing date.
  • Complete the sales disclosure form, which Indiana requires before the deed reaches the county auditor.
  • Gather permits and storm repair records if the home is near the river or in a tornado-hit area.
  • If you claim the homestead deduction, remember that a buyer who purchases after the assessment date can claim it by December 31 of the purchase year.

A cash offer for a Clark County house can close without repairs or showings, and the title company settles taxes from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Clark County property taxes are generally due May 10 and November 10. Copy A of the bill is paid in the spring and Copy B in the fall. Bills usually go out in early April.

faqs.q: Where is the Clark County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: The office is at 300 Corporate Drive, Suite 105, Jeffersonville, IN 47130, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It closes from noon to 1 p.m. Mail goes to PO Box 1689, Evansville, IN 47706.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Clark County tax sale property?
faqs.a: You have one year from the sale date. After that the bidder may seek a tax deed under Indiana Code. Redemption requires paying the amounts the statute sets, including interest.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Clark County?
faqs.a: The state deadline is June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed, using Form 130. File one petition per parcel. Check your Form 11 for the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clark County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure first, because penalties of 5% or 10% may apply.
